A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a new parameterisation for the flux and energy spectra of single and multiple atmospheric muons, which can be used as an input for a fast Monte Carlo simulation of atmospheric muon background.
we have developed an algorithm that can simulate the flux and the energy spectrum of single muons in the atmosphere, and the energy spectrum and lateral distributions of multiple muons.
we have provided an accurate and fast tool for the calculation of the muon flux, the lateral distribution and the energy spectrum of single or multiple muons in deep water or ice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral distribution of muons in the ice can be described by a simple function that is valid in a wide range of energies and zenith angles.

the muon energy is a good proxy of the muon multiplicity, and that the lateral distribution of single muons is well approximated by a Gaussian with a standard deviation that increases linearly with the muon energy.
the flux of muons in ice is about one order of magnitude lower than in water.
